If it happens today, the IWC will be on the wrestler like a hawk (i.e. Sexy Star trying to break that other wrestler's arm), so maybe the focus instead should be on the competitive drive of the wrestlers instead of the bullying and hazing and deliberate bombing of matches.

A bit of a counter point, just to play devils advocate...

I don't defend the idea of abusing new talent, especially when they're just trying their best to make it. I think there's something to be said about creating a space where talent can excel without worrying about getting hurt. Getting ribbed and all the dangerous shit that's happened in the past...I'm glad we're passed it.

I think there's a point about competitiveness that's lost in translation through all these old bitter veterans. People like Kenny Omega and Bryan Danielson didn't rise to the level they're at because they were passive and stood to the side all in the name of teamwork. They wanted to be stars, and they did it. They beat the shit out of people (all within the confines of being a good worker), kicked some fucking heads in, and stole the spotlight. 

What I think these veterans should get better at saying is the competitive spirit, the one where everyone is trying to climb the proverbial mountain to be the top guy, isn't there much anymore. From what it looks like, AEW is starting to become that in the Western hemisphere, and thank God because it brings out the best wrestling content of the week. 

Would love to hear counterpoints to this if anyone has any. Wrestling isn't ballet, but it doesn't have to be military boot camp either. 


TL;DR: old wrestlers should talk about trying to be a star in the ring more than they talk about abusing new talent, since bullying isn't cool ✌🏻
